headline: State desk: new licenses in Georgia, pre-rolls in Delaware, a store cap fight in Washington
dek: Five rule changes that open or close doors for operators this month.
body: Georgia will take medical dispensary license applications from 16 to 20 November, with its patient registry closing in on 65,000.

Delaware lets licensed growers make and wholesale their own non-infused pre-rolls from 11 November without a separate manufacturing license. Ohio now allows processors to turn packaged retail flower into concentrates and distillates.

Washington regulators are moving to stop chains from getting around the five-store ownership cap through shared branding and management deals. Alabama added two medical dispensaries, bringing its statewide total to five.
